course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
unit.description: Compare additive and multiplicative change, then build, compose, invert, and model with exponential and logarithmic functions, including residuals and semi-log plots.

variants.stem: Evaluate each expression without a calculator.

parts.prompt: Evaluate 9^(3/2).
Evaluate 9^(−1/2).

solution: 9^(3/2): the square root of 9 is 3, and 3 raised to the power 3 is 27.
9^(−1/2): the square root of 9 is 3, and 3 raised to the power −1 is 1/3.

variants.stem: The function f is given by f(x) = 6(2)ˣ, and the function g is given by g(x) = 6(2)^(x + 4). The graph of g can be described as a vertical dilation of the graph of f.

parts.prompt: By what factor is the graph of f dilated vertically to produce the graph of g?
Write g(x) in the form abˣ.

solution: The factor 2⁴ = 16 multiplies every output of f, so the graph of g is the graph of f dilated vertically by a factor of 16. In the form abˣ, g(x) = 96(2)ˣ.
